title: Feature-Flag Pollution
pattern: Interleaving conditional compilation attributes (`#[cfg(...)]`) directly inside core business logic or method bodies to toggle different platform behaviors.
why_bad: Severe visual noise and massive cognitive load. Developers must mentally parse multiple compilation branches simultaneously. It makes unit testing and static analysis highly fragile, as code code-paths are invisible to the compiler depending on which cargo flags are set.
detection: Look for `#[cfg(...)]` blocks inside function or method bodies, particularly when they enclose line-by-line alternative logic.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Low-level library code or platform abstraction boundaries (like standard library OS-specific file modules) where platform checks are unavoidable.
fix: Isolate the platform-dependent implementations behind a clean trait boundary, and conditionally compile the entire module or struct implementation file rather than inline statements.
source: *Robert C. Martin - Clean Code (2008)*, Chapter 3, "Functions"; *Titus Winters et al. - Software Engineering at Google (2020)*, Chapter 14, "Larger Testing" (Configuration vs Code).
